reason: Specification error: 3600 s is under two time constants of the room, so T cannot settle to 1e-3 of T_ss, and the below-critical filter on a crewed room leaves one case. The lock and the recorded FAIL stay (#185 (1), #187 (8)).

Specification error of the lead designer (#201 (2)): a 1e-3 K tolerance tighter than the kernel's own Euler error with a hold in the middle, and a < 15 % claim that the closed form itself puts at 43 %. Under the coolant-loop rule of #200 it fails differently; it was re-recorded canonically on the #200 kernel, so its record shows that kernel's FAIL (the replaced rule's FAIL is in the git history of its record).

Specification error of the lead designer (#201 (2)): case (c) 'below critical through 900 s' was estimated only until the reactor overheated, while decay heat kept flowing. Under #200 it fails differently (passive walls and life support keep every neighbour cool); it was re-recorded canonically on the #200 kernel, so its record shows that kernel's FAIL (the replaced rule's FAIL is in the git history of its record).

Superseded by the owner's design decision #200 (#201 (3)): its hold cases test one conductance for every wall; under the coolant-loop rule a beam bay | hold wall is passive and the hold cases fail. Locked and recorded with that FAIL.

Its target cell is destroyed, so under the D kernel it is never repaired (rate 0): the 15 cases with surviving quarters cells fail, the 5 with none (c = 0, no repair expected) still pass. Locked and recorded with that FAIL.
